page: Google Cloud Platform c4a-standard-72-lssd is a general-purpose server instance belonging to the c4a family. It is equipped with 72 dedicated vCPUs utilizing the arm64 CPU architecture. The system is configured with 288.0 GB of system memory, yielding a resource density of 4.0 GB of RAM per vCPU core. This configuration does not include graphics processing units or complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Although the instance name and basic description reference local solid-state drives, the primary configuration lists local storage as none, indicating that storage resources must be provisioned via network-attached block storage or specific storage attachments. The arm64 architecture provides energy-efficient multi-core processing suitable for scale-out workloads.

This server type is designed for general-purpose workloads that benefit from high core counts and a balanced memory-to-CPU ratio. Appropriate workloads include web serving, application servers, microservices architectures, containerized deployments, and multi-threaded development environments. From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the arm64 architecture typically offers a favorable performance-per-watt ratio, making it a viable option for resource-dense deployments that do not require x86-specific instruction sets.
